explanation: Many Germans remove their shoes at home and offer guests 'Hausschuhe' (house slippers), particularly in households with carpets, wood floors, or young children, but it isn't a strict universal rule and some hosts keep shoes on for more formal visits. The safest approach is to watch what your host does, or simply ask.
local_tip: If unsure, ask your host 'Soll ich die Schuhe ausziehen?' ('Should I take my shoes off?') when you arrive, or bring a clean pair of socks just in case.

also_check.note: Removing shoes indoors is mandatory, with dedicated house slippers and often separate ones for the bathroom.
Shoe removal varies widely by household and region; it's often optional unless the host asks.
Shoes are routinely removed at the door, with slippers commonly offered to guests.

sources.title: Why We Don't Wear Shoes in Our Home - ourgabledhome.com
